title: optimization-search-policy
summary: Policy for how an optimization agent should select, order, and stop optimization experiments. Covers candidate generation, exploration vs exploitation, diversity, negative experiment memory, budget allocation, and stopping criteria. Drawn from vllm-evolve (phase-locked optimization round), TRT-LLM casebook (prior-art matching), and SkillOpt (bounded edit + gate). Use when deciding what to try next and when to stop.

skill_metadata.name: optimization-search-policy
skill_metadata.description: Policy for how an optimization agent should select, order, and stop optimization experiments. Covers candidate generation, exploration vs exploitation, diversity, negative experiment memory, budget allocation, and stopping criteria. Drawn from vllm-evolve (phase-locked optimization round), TRT-LLM casebook (prior-art matching), and SkillOpt (bounded edit + gate). Use when deciding what to try next and when to stop.

applicability.scope: Selecting, ordering and stopping optimization experiments: candidate generation, exploration versus exploitation, mechanism diversity, negative experiment memory, cost-aware escalation, budget allocation and stopping criteria, drawn from vllm-evolve, the TRT-LLM casebook and SkillOpt
applicability.prerequisites: The useful work, quality contract, allowed approximations, timing boundary and resource budget are frozen before search, and a complete restartable incumbent is preserved; reading the procedures authorizes no execution, framework change, new resource spending or publication
applicability.input_contract: Profiling data, existing config, prior experiment and negative records and the casebook for the current bottleneck class, model and hardware; each target stage's fraction of E2E time; the target, locally measured uncertainty and the authorized budget
applicability.produced_artifact: An ordered experiment plan: one candidate change per round with an explicit hypothesis and its motivating evidence, a bounded shortlist of distinct mechanisms with assumptions, uncertainty, expected impact and evaluation cost, negative records turned into search constraints, and a stop-or-switch decision; when authorized rounds run, a recorded verdict per round with best-seen and delivered outcomes kept apart
failure_modes: The evaluation protocol, measurement setup or baseline changes in the same round as the candidate
Benchmark budget is spent on a candidate that fails correctness
A matching keyword in a rejection record is used as a causal diagnosis or automatic veto, or one failed implementation excludes a whole solution family
Expensive work starts on a stage without computing its Amdahl contribution, so a large local speedup yields little E2E gain
One mechanism family keeps being sampled only because budget remains, without re-profiling after the limiting stage moves
Roofline proximity or a utilization threshold is used as a universal stopping rule
Screening is allowed to skip the frozen acceptance regimes or required service-level evidence
applicability.refusal_point: Discards a correctness-breaking, worse or inconclusive change instead of integrating it, preserves no-change when candidates cannot be separated, does not count a shortcut outside the authorized semantics as an optimization, and does not let a successful probe qualify a broken final state

recommendations: Before generating a candidate, consult the casebook, the negative record and the target stage's Amdahl contribution.
Record every worse or inconclusive result with hypothesis, metric, context, evidence level and failure type, and derive a search constraint from it.
When about three experiments on one hypothesis return inconclusive from measurement variance, fix the protocol or move to a different hypothesis.
Before reporting, restore and verify the best fully valid incumbent through its canonical launcher.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
